before_booking.intro_line: Four things buyers ask about before the first cheque, with the rules behind them.
before_booking.note_line: General information, not legal, tax or financial advice.

payment_plans.title: Which payment plan?
payment_plans.sub: Construction-linked, down payment or subvention, and what each one risks.

paras.text: You pay each stage once it is built, so your money follows the building. Check each demand against the latest QPR.
You pay most of the price early, often for a discount. If the project is late, more of your money waits with it. Before a registered agreement, the law still caps you at 10%.
The bank pays the developer early, and the developer promises to pay your pre-EMI. You are still the borrower: if the developer stops paying, the bank collects from you.
get the lender's confirmation in writing: what it pays out, when, and who pays the pre-EMI if the developer stops.

loans.title: Home loans
loans.sub: Loan checks arrive in 2027. What to check with your bank now.

paras.text: Plinth doesn't arrange loans or pass your number to any lender today.
is this project approved by your bank? Ask the bank, in writing, not the developer.

paras.lead: Banks usually don't lend for stamp duty or registration.
paras.text: Plan for those from your own money.

nri.title: Buying from abroad (NRI)
nri.sub: Paying from NRE or NRO, a power of attorney, and FEMA basics.

paras.text: From an NRE, FCNR(B) or NRO account, or money sent to India through a bank. FEMA doesn't allow paying in foreign currency notes or traveller's cheques.
Indian banks lend to NRIs. EMIs come from an NRE or NRO account.
Like any buyer, you deduct 1% from each instalment when the price is ₹50 L or more (s.194-IA). You need a PAN.

Make it specific to this flat, and list what your relative may sign: booking form, agreement, payments, registration. One signed abroad is attested at an Indian mission or apostilled, then stamped in India within 3 months.

selling_before_possession.title: Selling before possession
selling_before_possession.sub: Transfer charges, the builder's NOC and what RERA says.

paras.text: Selling before possession means transferring your allotment. The developer endorses the new buyer on your agreement and issues a no-objection certificate (NOC).
whoever takes your allotment becomes the allottee, with your rights, including delay interest (s.2(d)).
about capital-gains tax, and a lawyer about stamp duty on the transfer.
Our resale and transfer checks are planned for Apr–Jun 2027.
